newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans fall in fast trade as funds sell.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans fall in fast trade as funds sell.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures were sharply lower with the May and July contracts in fast dealings on heavy fund selling, traders said.
Sell stops were hit below $8.40 per bushel in the May contract.
Griffin Trading reportedly sold 2.5 million bushels of soybeans and 1,200 lots of soymeal.

Fundamentally, traders cited Brazilian denials of market rumors of a plan to impose an export tax on soybeans. Brazilian crushers and the Brazilian Agricultural Ministry on Friday dismissed talk of such a plan, saying it was unlikely and would be opposed by the ministry if proposed.
The tax would have made Brazilian soybeans more expensive and encouraged world buyers to purchase U.S. supplies, floor traders said.
At 1141 CST, soybeans were down 17 to 4-1/2 cents per bushel with May off 13 at $8.36-1/2. Soymeal was down $5.70 to $2.40 per ton with May down $5.20 at $269.50.
